text:
Aisha: FYI — BrightlineX procurement pushed back asking for final SLO evidence before signing. They want uptime >= 99.9% and p95 embeddings latency <= 150ms. Can CS + Eng Ops assemble an evidence packet and a mitigation plan by EOD?
Liam: short answer: we can show monthly uptime and incident delta, but p95 at current config is ~230ms for embeddings. latency win needs routing + kv-cache warmup. :thinking_face:
Carlos: agree with Liam. We can offer a canary on m1-fast (.fp16 + optimized kernels) which drops p95 to ~140–160ms in our lab runs. Need approval for a short dedicated burst.
Nora: procurement deadline is today 18:00 PT. If we can't present a clear plan + numbers they may push renewal or ask for bigger credits. I flagged renewal risk.
Sam: I can produce the monitoring slices and a short runbook. Will attach the queries/plots. Quick Prom query for p95 embeddings:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/embed"}[5m])) by (le))
```
And uptime window (30d):
```
sum(up{job="redwood-api"} == 1) / count_over_time(up{job="redwood-api"}[30d])
```
Carlos: For customer packet propose: 1) uptime attestation + 30d graph 2) p95 current vs mitigated plan 3) recommended short-term mitigations (canary, prefix cache, batch size tweaks) 4) credit calc if we miss SLO 5) rollout timeline (72h for canary + 48h monitoring).
Aisha: Perfect. Nora — can you lead customer comms? Ask them if they accept canary + 72h monitoring as a condition. If yes, we frame credits as "last-resort" and emphasize mitigation.
Nora: On it. I’ll ask now and paste the reply.
onboard-bot: Reminder: attach onboarding playbook checklist and any past uptime attestations to reduce procurement friction.
Liam: I'll put together the metrics export and a short doc with the Prom queries + sample graphs. ETA 2h.
Carlos: I'll draft the technical note on canary config and estimated cost impact of burst.
Sam: I'll prepare the runbook and list of dashboard links + trace samples.
Aisha: Thanks team — if we get green from customer we escalate to Dedicated capacity request and Ops will schedule the canary. If they decline, we prepare a conservative credit calc and the exec comms. :thumbsup:
Nora: Reply from BrightlineX: they'd prefer a short canary and a "no-penalty" hold on credits while we monitor. Asking for the packet immediately. Sending their procurement contact.
Aisha: Great — I'll compile everything into a single PDF and shared folder. Tag me when drafts are ready.
Liam: Drafts in #eng-sre will be linked. I'll also include raw traces for the last 7 days.
Carlos: Draft canary config attached to the doc: routing rule -> m1-fast when region == us-west-2 and token_count < 1024, kv-cache warmup enabled.
Aisha: Awesome. Meeting to review packet at 16:00 PT in case any edits.
Nora: Confirmed. I'll update the procurement thread with our plan and the 16:00 review invite.
Aisha: Thanks everyone — this is high-priority for renewal.
